title: Fast Fashion Environmental Impact

title: Renewable Energy Transition Barriers

title: Urban Food Desert

title: Species Habitat Fragmentation

title: Climate Misinformation Spread

title: Loss Of Indigenous Land Rights
brief: Indigenous communities are losing custodianship of lands they have sustainably managed for generations, leading to ecological damage.

title: Transport Emissions Lock-In
brief: Car-dependent city planning and slow EV transition are keeping transport as a major source of emissions.

title: Food Price Spike
brief: Food prices are surging globally. Lower-income communities are most at risk.

title: Climate Migration
brief: Millions are being displaced by climate impacts — floods, droughts and rising seas.

title: Ocean Acidification

title: Glacier Retreat

title: Groundwater Depletion

title: Urban Heat Island

title: Wildfire Risk
brief: Hotter, drier conditions are expanding wildfire seasons and increasing fire intensity.

title: Pollinator Loss

title: Mangrove Loss

title: Supply Chain Disruption

title: AI Energy Consumption Crisis

title: Algorithmic Greenwashing
brief: AI & SUSTAINABILITY MYSTERY   ·   This mystery explores the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and climate action.

title: Insurance Crisis

title: Desertification

title: Ecosystem Collapse
brief: Interconnected ecological systems are failing as keystone species disappear and food webs unravel.

title: Coastal Erosion
brief: Rising sea levels and intensifying storms are eating away coastlines, threatening communities and infrastructure.

title: Energy Security Crisis

title: Infrastructure Failure
brief: Ageing or climate-damaged infrastructure is breaking down, disrupting communities and economies.

title: Public Health Emergency

title: Climate Refugees

title: Fisheries Collapse
brief: Commercial fish stocks are collapsing under the combined pressure of overfishing and climate change.

title: Water Conflict
brief: Shrinking freshwater resources are fuelling international and community-level conflict.

title: AI-Driven Resource Extraction Surge
brief: AI optimisation tools are making fossil fuel and mineral extraction dramatically more efficient and profitable, accelerating environmental damage beyond what regulation can keep pace with.

title: Autonomous Systems & Ecological Blind Spots
brief: Autonomous drones, precision agriculture AI and smart infrastructure are making decisions that damage ecosystems and wildlife corridors without any ecological awareness built into their design.

title: Economic Instability
brief: Climate shocks and transition costs are destabilising global financial systems.

title: Social Inequality
brief: Climate change is deepening wealth and power gaps, with the poorest hit hardest and least able to adapt.

title: Food System Breakdown
brief: The global food system is fracturing under climate, economic and ecological pressures.

title: Biodiversity Collapse
brief: The sixth mass extinction is accelerating as ecosystems unravel globally.

title: Carbon Lock-In
brief: Fossil fuel infrastructure and economic dependency are preventing the clean energy transition.

title: Tipping Point Activation
brief: Self-reinforcing feedback loops in the climate system are being triggered — reversal may be impossible.

title: Amazon Dieback
brief: The Amazon rainforest is approaching a tipping point beyond which it converts to savanna.
aiConnection: Training large AI models can consume as much electricity as hundreds of homes use in a year. As AI scales globally, data-centre demand could reach 10–20% of world electricity by 2030, AI's climate benefit depends entirely on whether its energy source is clean.

title: Ocean Circulation Disruption
brief: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is weakening, threatening global weather patterns.
aiConnection: Generative AI makes it trivially easy to produce convincing sustainability reports and fabricated impact metrics at scale. Without mandatory AI audit trails and third-party ESG verification, bad actors can flood markets with false green claims, diverting billions from genuine climate solutions.

title: Multi-Hazard Cascades
brief: Multiple simultaneous climate crises are compounding each other beyond humanity's ability to respond.
aiConnection: AI is being deployed by oil, gas and mining companies to locate previously uneconomical reserves and optimise drilling, producing a rebound effect where efficiency gains accelerate total extraction. The same tools that could model climate futures are making fossil-fuel exploitation cheaper and faster, a direct contradiction of decarbonisation goals.

title: Planetary Boundaries Breach
brief: FINAL CHALLENGE: Earth is exceeding safe operating limits. The future of civilisation is at stake.
aiConnection: Most AI systems optimising logistics, agriculture and urban planning are trained on economic and efficiency data only, with no ecological constraints encoded. Autonomous decisions can systematically destroy pollinator habitat, fragment wildlife corridors or disrupt migration patterns at scale, faster than any human process and with no single point of accountability.

title: AI Climate Model Manipulation
brief: State and corporate actors are using adversarial AI to inject systematic errors into shared climate models, corrupting the scientific consensus underpinning global climate agreements.
aiConnection: Modern climate science depends on shared AI-driven models, CMIP6, weather prediction, carbon-cycle models, feeding directly into IPCC reports. Adversarial machine learning can introduce subtle, undetectable biases that make models systematically underestimate warming or overstate carbon sinks, one of the highest-stakes AI security threats on the planet.

title: AI-Accelerated Inequality in Climate Adaptation
brief: Wealthy nations and corporations are using AI to gain massive adaptation advantages — precision flood prediction, AI-optimised crop systems, smart city resilience — while the Global South is left entirely behind, deepening the climate justice gap to a breaking point.
aiConnection: Precision flood prediction, AI-optimised crop systems and smart-city resilience require data, compute, and talent concentrated in the Global North. Without deliberate transfer mechanisms, AI compounds existing climate injustice, those least responsible for emissions have the least access to the tools that reduce harm.
